history.summary: CSV FLAG: this temple is NOT in Chandigarh - it stands on a hillock at Jayanti Majri (Majrian) village, about 15 km from Chandigarh, in Mohali district, Punjab (some sources say Ropar district - verify current district boundary). Jayanti Devi is one of the seven sister goddesses of the Kangra Valley (with Naina Devi, Jawalamukhi, Chintpurni, Mansa Devi, Brajeshwari and Chamunda Devi). Legend says a princess of Kangra, married into the Hathnaur estate north of present-day Chandigarh, brought the goddess with her; the King of Hathnaur built the temple on the hill, and it was later renovated by Garibdas (Garibu). The temple is reached by about 100 steps; at the base lies a large water tank and an ancient well said to give sweet water year-round. Villagers of Jayanti Majri restrict their houses to a single storey out of respect for the goddess. A small Jayanti Dam nearby attracts migratory birds. The 550-600-year age rests on oral tradition and the temple signboard (verify against archaeology).

name: Jayanti Devi Temple
town: Jayanti Majri (Mohali district) (CSV town 'Chandigarh' is imprecise - the temple is ~15 km from Chandigarh)
town_description: Jayanti Majri is a village near Mullanpur/New Chandigarh in Mohali district, Punjab, at the Shivalik foothills on the bank of the seasonal Jayanti Rao rivulet. Surrounded by fields and mango groves, the village owes its name to the hillock temple. Nearby attractions include the Jayanti Dam (birding spot), Sukhna Lake and Nada Sahib Gurdwara in Chandigarh.

travel.road: About 15 km from Chandigarh city via Kansal/Mullanpur; metalled road to the base of the hillock, nearest bus stop Jayanti Majri (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; February (annual full-moon fair) and Navratri for festivals - very crowded then.
